paper_type: retracted referred pediatric case series with retrospective exposure timing
reader_conclusion: The publication describes 12 referred children with gastrointestinal abnormalities and developmental regression and reports that parents or physicians temporally associated behavioral onset with MMR vaccination in eight cases. As a case series, that design could never establish an MMR-autism causal effect. More importantly for the present audit, the article was fully retracted and later investigations documented discrepancies between published case histories and underlying records, so the central temporal-trigger evidence cannot be treated as a trustworthy inspectable substrate merely because the published narrative remains readable.
not_applicable_reason: The central exposure-timing and case-history evidence has a documented source-integrity failure, and the referred case-series design supplies no independent comparator capable of rescuing the causal inference.

usable.results: The paper remains useful as a historical record of a 12-child referred case series and as an example of how temporal anecdotes can be presented alongside clinical findings.
usable.methods_or_design: It is a strong teaching case for why referred case series, retrospective exposure attribution, and temporal ordering cannot establish vaccine causation.
usable.materials_or_documentation: The published article, partial interpretation retraction, full retraction, and later record-based investigations form a well-documented integrity and inference case.

downweight.worth_noticing: Some gastrointestinal and developmental observations were presented as clinical findings, but they do not create an epidemiologic comparison and cannot independently establish an MMR trigger.
downweight.cautious_or_ignore: Do not reuse the reported MMR timing or the paper's trigger narrative as evidence for a causal MMR-autism association; the case-series design is inadequate and the relevant case-history substrate was later formally discredited.

uncertainty_and_follow_up: The causal question requires population-level comparative epidemiology with reliable vaccination and developmental records. That evidence must come from independent studies rather than attempting to repair this retracted case series.
